input.body:
Weekly wiki-growth pass (web mode — WebSearch available; WebFetch is blocked at this environment's network egress proxy for every publisher domain involved, which is itself a correction to what the pages previously recorded).

## Questions researched

Both touched pages had the same standing top open question, so this pass spot-checked citations rather than opening new ground:

1. **audience/** — *"Re-verify the Gartner and trust-signal figures at source."*
2. **consulting-market/** — *"Re-verify the market-size, CAGR, segment-growth and pricing figures at source."*

Both re-verifications came back as **corrections, not confirmations**. Neither page had a figure that survived unchanged.

## What changed, and where

### `product-wiki/audience/README.md`

- **Correction:** the 67% rep-free figure carries a qualifier the first pass dropped — Gartner's headline is 67% prefer a rep-free experience **"for at least part of their purchase."** The page stated it flatly. Correction recorded in the body with its why; the header bullet rewritten to carry the qualifier.
- **Correction:** the 2026 release's sample (n=646, fielded Aug–Sep 2025) is *not* the n=632 / Aug–Sep 2024 sample behind the 69% website-vs-seller and 73% outreach figures — that sample belongs to the 2025 release. Both are now stated explicitly so they can't be read as interchangeable.
- **New section, "The validation paradox, and the AI reader."** A *later* Gartner release the page had not seen (2026-05-20, n=645) inverts its top-line reading: in the same buyer population, **70% prefer a completely digital self-service experience** *and* **69% prefer to validate AI-generated insights with a sales rep.** So rep-free buying is not the unambiguous good news the first pass recorded for a firm with no sales team — buyers self-serve the research and then want a human to confirm it. That validation moment currently has no owner on this site, which is a requirement, not a nice-to-have. (Explicitly disambiguated in the body from the *other* 69% already on the page — two unrelated Gartner findings landing on the same number.)
- **New finding:** buyers used an **average of seven information sources**, and **45% used GenAI, primarily to gather vendor and product information**. For a large minority of visits the site's first reader is a model summarising it for the buyer — so claims carried by layout rather than by text degrade through that channel. Partly answers the standing "what do they search for on the way" question: increasingly they don't search, they ask.
- Header: flat 67% bullet rewritten; two bullets added (7 total, at the cap).
- Citation caveat corrected: the cause is this environment's **egress proxy**, not publisher 403s as first recorded — `gartner.com`, `digitalcommerce360.com`, `demandgenreport.com` and `businesswire.com` are all unreachable here, so no primary *or* secondary carriage is directly readable and re-verification at source needs a human.

### `product-wiki/consulting-market/README.md`

- **Superseded (not deleted, with its why):** the "$14.1bn in 2026 → $116.81bn by 2035 at ~26.5% CAGR" headline was **misattributed**. Fortune Business Insights' current report says **$11.91bn in 2026 → $73.89bn by 2034 at 25.6%**. The $14.08bn / 26.49% pairing the first pass rounded belongs to **Business Research Insights**, a different firm. The **$116.81bn-by-2035 endpoint could not be reproduced from any source found** and is marked unverified rather than removed.
- **The larger finding, now a table in the body:** four firms' 2026 estimates for the same named market span **$11.91bn to $38.7bn (3.3x)** with CAGRs from **18.4% to 35.8%**. That's a disagreement about what "AI consulting services" includes, not measurement noise. The page now states that **no unattributed headline market-size number is quotable** — a more useful answer to "re-verify at source" than a confirmation would have been.
- **Re-confirmed:** SMB AI consulting growing ~25.7% annually, outpacing enterprise. Unaffected by the spread, and the positioning argument built on it still stands.
- **New, against the standing geography question:** North America is **38.13% of the 2025 market**. So the US-centricity of every source this wiki has found is not evidence the market is American — the majority of the category sits outside the sources' focus.
- Header: market-size bullet rewritten to the spread; geography bullet added (7 total, at the cap).
- Citation caveat corrected (same egress-proxy cause), and the pricing benchmarks explicitly flagged as **not** re-checked this pass.

`product-wiki/brand/README.md` was read end to end and **deliberately left untouched** — this pass surfaced nothing citable for it, and padding it would be worse than leaving it.

## Citations added

audience/:
- https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-05-20-gartner-survey-finds-sixty-nine-percent-of-b-two-b-buyers-turn-to-sales-reps-to-validate-ai-generated-insights — the validation finding, 70% fully-digital, 45% GenAI, seven-sources average, n=645 / Aug–Sep 2025
- https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2026/03/17/gartner-b2b-buyers-rep-free-purchasing-ai-reshapes-sales/ — n=646 / Aug–Sep 2025 and the "at least part of their purchase" qualifier
- https://www.demandgenreport.com/industry-news/news-brief/gartner-67-of-b2b-buyers-prefer-a-rep-free-experience/52142/ — second independent report of the same release
- https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260520585188/en/Gartner-Survey-Finds-69-of-B2B-Buyers-Turn-to-Sales-Reps-to-Validate-AI-Generated-Insights — wire carriage of the May release
- (existing 2025 Gartner release annotated as the origin of the n=632 / Aug–Sep 2024 sample)

consulting-market/:
- https://www.businessresearchinsights.com/market-reports/ai-consulting-services-market-119843 — $14.08bn / 26.49%, the actual origin of the first pass's headline
- https://markwideresearch.com/ai-consulting-services-market — $38.7bn 2026 → $176.96bn 2035 at 18.40%
- (Fortune Business Insights and Market Data Forecast entries re-annotated with their current, corrected figures)

**Every figure above is attributed from search-result summaries, corroborated across independent searches — not read at source, because this environment cannot fetch any of these domains.** That is recorded on both pages rather than glossed, and it is why this lands as an unmerged PR for review.

## Open questions left for the next run

Added by this pass:
- With 45% of buyers researching via GenAI, is this site legible to a model reading it on a buyer's behalf, and what specifically would make it more so?
- Who supplies the human validation moment 69% of buyers want, when there is no sales team — is a named founder with a real reply address enough, or does it take a bookable call?
- If the site cites a market size at all, whose definition of "AI consulting services" does it adopt?
- Where does the unverified "$116.81bn by 2035" figure come from? Nothing found this pass reproduces it.
- Re-verify the pricing benchmarks ($5k–$25k per project, $150–$350/hr) — untouched since the first pass, and now the only figures on that page with a single unchecked origin.

Sharpened rather than removed:
- Re-verification at source is **not achievable by any agent pass here** while the egress proxy blocks the publishers; it needs a human or an unblocked environment.
- Geography: North America is only 38% of the market — where does Missing Bulb actually sell?

Untouched and still open: the regulated-category question, the referral-path question, the first-screen question, the substitute-proof question, and consulting-market's wedge, published-pricing, category-definition and direct-small-competitor questions.

No requirement was moved — `product-wiki/product-requirements/` is untouched, per the isolation rule. The validation-moment finding is the one most likely to want a requirement change, and it waits for a human here.

{"number":103,"title":"product-wiki growth 2026-08-09: re-verification found two misstated citations","body":"Weekly wiki-growth pass (web mode — WebSearch available; WebFetch is blocked at this environment's network egress proxy for every publisher domain involved, which is itself a correction to what the pages previously recorded).

## Questions researched

Both touched pages had the same standing top open question, so this pass spot-checked citations rather than opening new ground:

1. **audience/** — *"Re-verify the Gartner and trust-signal figures at source."*
2. **consulting-market/** — *"Re-verify the market-size, CAGR, segment-growth and pricing figures at source."*

Both re-verifications came back as **corrections, not confirmations**. Neither page had a figure that survived unchanged.

## What changed, and where

### `product-wiki/audience/README.md`

- **Correction:** the 67% rep-free figure carries a qualifier the first pass dropped — Gartner's headline is 67% prefer a rep-free experience **"for at least part of their purchase."** The page stated it flatly. Correction recorded in the body with its why; the header bullet rewritten to carry the qualifier.
- **Correction:** the 2026 release's sample (n=646, fielded Aug–Sep 2025) is *not* the n=632 / Aug–Sep 2024 sample behind the 69% website-vs-seller and 73% outreach figures — that sample belongs to the 2025 release. Both are now stated explicitly so they can't be read as interchangeable.
- **New section, "The validation paradox, and the AI reader."** A *later* Gartner release the page had not seen (2026-05-20, n=645) inverts its top-line reading: in the same buyer population, **70% prefer a completely digital self-service experience** *and* **69% prefer to validate AI-generated insights with a sales rep.** So rep-free buying is not the unambiguous good news the first pass recorded for a firm with no sales team — buyers self-serve the research and then want a human to confirm it. That validation moment currently has no owner on this site, which is a requirement, not a nice-to-have. (Explicitly disambiguated in the body from the *other* 69% already on the page — two unrelated Gartner findings landing on the same number.)
- **New finding:** buyers used an **average of seven information sources**, and **45% used GenAI, primarily to gather vendor and product information**. For a large minority of visits the site's first reader is a model summarising it for the buyer — so claims carried by layout rather than by text degrade through that channel. Partly answers the standing "what do they search for on the way" question: increasingly they don't search, they ask.
- Header: flat 67% bullet rewritten; two bullets added (7 total, at the cap).
- Citation caveat corrected: the cause is this environment's **egress proxy**, not publisher 403s as first recorded — `gartner.com`, `digitalcommerce360.com`, `demandgenreport.com` and `businesswire.com` are all unreachable here, so no primary *or* secondary carriage is directly readable and re-verification at source needs a human.

### `product-wiki/consulting-market/README.md`

- **Superseded (not deleted, with its why):** the "$14.1bn in 2026 → $116.81bn by 2035 at ~26.5% CAGR" headline was **misattributed**. Fortune Business Insights' current report says **$11.91bn in 2026 → $73.89bn by 2034 at 25.6%**. The $14.08bn / 26.49% pairing the first pass rounded belongs to **Business Research Insights**, a different firm. The **$116.81bn-by-2035 endpoint could not be reproduced from any source found** and is marked unverified rather than removed.
- **The larger finding, now a table in the body:** four firms' 2026 estimates for the same named market span **$11.91bn to $38.7bn (3.3x)** with CAGRs from **18.4% to 35.8%**. That's a disagreement about what "AI consulting services" includes, not measurement noise. The page now states that **no unattributed headline market-size number is quotable** — a more useful answer to "re-verify at source" than a confirmation would have been.
- **Re-confirmed:** SMB AI consulting growing ~25.7% annually, outpacing enterprise. Unaffected by the spread, and the positioning argument built on it still stands.
- **New, against the standing geography question:** North America is **38.13% of the 2025 market**. So the US-centricity of every source this wiki has found is not evidence the market is American — the majority of the category sits outside the sources' focus.
- Header: market-size bullet rewritten to the spread; geography bullet added (7 total, at the cap).
- Citation caveat corrected (same egress-proxy cause), and the pricing benchmarks explicitly flagged as **not** re-checked this pass.

`product-wiki/brand/README.md` was read end to end and **deliberately left untouched** — this pass surfaced nothing citable for it, and padding it would be worse than leaving it.

## Citations added

audience/:
- ``https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-05-20-gartner-survey-finds-sixty-nine-percent-of-b-two-b-buyers-turn-to-sales-reps-to-validate-ai-generated-insights`` — the validation finding, 70% fully-digital, 45% GenAI, seven-sources average, n=645 / Aug–Sep 2025
- https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2026/03/17/gartner-b2b-buyers-rep-free-purchasing-ai-reshapes-sales/ — n=646 / Aug–Sep 2025 and the "at least part of their purchase" qualifier
- https://www.demandgenreport.com/industry-news/news-brief/gartner-67-of-b2b-buyers-prefer-a-rep-free-experience/52142/ — second independent report of the same release
- ``https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260520585188/en/Gartner-Survey-Finds-69-of-B2B-Buyers-Turn-to-Sales-Reps-to-Validate-AI-Generated-Insights`` — wire carriage of the May release
- (existing 2025 Gartner release annotated as the origin of the n=632 / Aug–Sep 2024 sample)

consulting-market/:
- https://www.businessresearchinsights.com/market-reports/ai-consulting-services-market-119843 — $14.08bn / 26.49%, the actual origin of the first pass's headline
- https://markwideresearch.com/ai-consulting-services-market — $38.7bn 2026 → $176.96bn 2035 at 18.40%
- (Fortune Business Insights and Market Data Forecast entries re-annotated with their current, corrected figures)

**Every figure above is attributed from search-result summaries, corroborated across independent searches — not read at source, because this environment cannot fetch any of these domains.** That is recorded on both pages rather than glossed, and it is why this lands as an unmerged PR for review.

## Open questions left for the next run

Added by this pass:
- With 45% of buyers researching via GenAI, is this site legible to a model reading it on a buyer's behalf, and what specifically would make it more so?
- Who supplies the human validation moment 69% of buyers want, when there is no sales team — is a named founder with a real reply address enough, or does it take a bookable call?
- If the site cites a market size at all, whose definition of "AI consulting services" does it adopt?
- Where does the unverified "$116.81bn by 2035" figure come from? Nothing found this pass reproduces it.
- Re-verify the pricing benchmarks ($5k–$25k per project, $150–$350/hr) — untouched since the first pass, and now the only figures on that page with a single unchecked origin.

Sharpened rather than removed:
- Re-verification at source is **not achievable by any agent pass here** while the egress proxy blocks the publishers; it needs a human or an unblocked environment.
- Geography: North America is only 38% of the market — where does Missing Bulb actually sell?

Untouched and still open: the regulated-category question, the referral-path question, the first-screen question, the substitute-proof question, and consulting-market's wedge, published-pricing, category-definition and direct-small-competitor questions.

No requirement was moved — `product-wiki/product-requirements/` is untouched, per the isolation rule. The validation-moment finding is the one most likely to want a requirement change, and it waits for a human here.
